chunks: What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman and Hisham ibn Salim, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would pronounce five takbirs over some people and four over others; and when he pronounced four takbirs over a man, he was regarded with suspicion.

key_terms.أَرْبَعًا: four takbirs recited over the dead
key_terms.اتُّهِمَ: he was suspected or regarded with doubt
key_terms.خَمْسًا: five takbirs recited over the dead
key_terms.قَوْمٍ: a group of people or deceased persons
key_terms.يُكَبِّرُ: to pronounce the takbir in the funeral prayer

ai.seo_question: Why did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم say five takbirs over some deceased persons and four over others?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم performed different numbers of takbirs over the dead, giving five for some and four for others. It indicates a distinction in funeral prayer practice and suggests that receiving only four takbirs carried a negative implication about the deceased.
